name: K-8 Student Club Volunteers @Locke
description: Help Lead our K-8 School Clubs at Locke! Each of our students is involved in clubs to explore new interests, build skills through hands-on projects, or develop their leadership skills. School clubs are divided by grade: K-2, 3-5, or 6-8. Examples of clubs include animal care, soccer, arts & crafts, farming, printmaking, advanced dance, and model UN. School staff members lead the clubs, but we need volunteers to support students' learning and joy! In all cases, volunteers create a welcoming environment for students and assist with student engagement. In some cases, volunteers may provide expertise-based lessons, depending on the club. Clubs take place every Thursday from 1:30-3pm when school is in session, tentatively beginning in October. We ask that volunteers make a weekly commitment. Ready to get involved? Click "Respond" to start the process of signing up. Volunteers will be prompted to upload their signed documents and clearances, if they have not already. Clearances are valid for 5 years. As part of the sign-up process, you will also be invited to speak with our team about which club is the best fit. You can also reach out to our Volunteer Coordinator, Maddie, (CommSchools@Phila.gov) to express interest in volunteering and ask questions about the sign-up process.

Volunteers are needed to help with picking up trash, weeding, planting, watering and more. Volunteers should come dressed to work outside in the garden, preferably in closed toe shoes. We have some gardening tools at the school but also invite volunteers to bring their own. Hours : We host occasional scheduled Community Garden Work Nights with our partners at the Audubon Society. We also appreciate volunteers who can stop by the garden on a regular basis to help keep it in good shape. Volunteers can work with our staff to schedule good times to come by the garden. Location : at the front of Gideon School Requirements : Volunteers need to sign the School District Code of Conduct and Volunteer Waiver. You will be asked to upload these, if you have not already, when signing up. These are valid for at least 5 years. Ready to Get Involved? Click "Respond" to start the sign-up process. Our team will reach out to you with any scheduled work nights and more information about supporting the garden. Please reach out to the Volunteer Coordinator, Maddie, with any questions about signing up (CommSchools@Phila.gov).

description: Sign up through SurveyMonkey: Dunbar Volunteer Sign Up . Join us to give out free groceries to the Dunbar community on one Friday a month! Volunteers are needed to pass out free groceries and fresh produce to the community. We have a food distribution 1x month on a Friday, with volunteers coming for either the 9am-12pm shift or 12pm-2pm shift. name: City of Philadelphia - Philly Reading Coaches
description: Who We Are: Philly Reading Coaches (PRC) is an afterschool early literacy program funded by the Office of Children and Families and implemented by Out-of-School time (OST) providers. This is a unique chance for volunteers to make a real impact in their community and build meaningful connections with young learners by making reading exciting and fun! PRC takes place at 13 schools around the city. Click here to browse PRC Opportunities! | What We Do: PRC’s model combines early reading support, access to books, and civic engagement to strengthen foundational literacy skills and encourage a love of reading for our city's children. Philly Reading Coaches pairs volunteers to read one-on-one with kindergarten-3rd grade students for 1-2 hours per week after school from October to May. Our aim is to boost reading motivation and confidence for our city's young readers. Click here to create an account and get started! For step-by-step instructions, follow this guide & Sign up for orientation HERE *When your qualifications have been approved, click here respond to the opportunity/ies of your choice to sign up for shifts.
